content.value_statement: Reasoning models can spend many tokens on repeated self-reflection. This skill shows how to suppress selected reflection tokens during inference.
actual_capabilities: Explains when the NOWAIT technique is useful for reasoning-model inference.
Provides a Python logit processor for suppressing reflection-related tokenizer IDs.
Lists default reflection keywords and excluded false-positive patterns.
Shows integration patterns for HuggingFace Transformers and vLLM workflows.
Includes helper functions for generation, bad words IDs, and stopping criteria.
limitations: It assumes users already have a compatible model, tokenizer, and inference stack.
It may reduce accuracy on distilled models or tasks that need longer verification.
Keyword lists may need model-specific tuning before production use.
Benchmark claims should be validated on the user's own workload.

prompt_templates.title: Explain NOWAIT Basics

prompt_templates.title: Design a Production Evaluation

output_examples.input: I want to reduce token usage for QwQ-32B reasoning answers.
output_examples.output: A concise plan comparing baseline output length, NOWAIT output length, latency, cost, and answer accuracy on representative prompts.

output_examples.input: My distilled Qwen model loses accuracy after suppression.
output_examples.output: A troubleshooting summary recommending softer suppression, fewer keywords, and task-specific evaluation before continued use.

output_examples.input: I need to integrate NOWAIT into an existing generation service.
output_examples.output: An implementation checklist covering tokenizer setup, processor placement, monitoring metrics, and rollback conditions.

best_practices: Measure answer quality and token savings together before using suppression in production.
Start with RL-based reasoning models and validate distilled models separately.
Keep a baseline configuration available so teams can compare and revert quickly.
anti_patterns: Do not suppress reflection tokens for tasks where careful verification is required.
Do not assume the default keyword list fits every tokenizer or language.
Do not report token savings without checking answer correctness.

faq.question: What does this skill optimize?
faq.answer: It helps reduce repeated reflection tokens in reasoning-model outputs during inference.

faq.question: Does it train or fine-tune a model?
faq.answer: No. It applies inference-time token suppression and does not modify model weights.

faq.question: Which tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: The report lists Claude, Codex, and Claude Code as supported tools.

faq.question: Can this hurt answer quality?
faq.answer: Yes. Distilled models and hard tasks may need reflection tokens for accurate reasoning.

faq.question: Does the included script make network requests?
faq.answer: No evidence of network requests was found in the script. Example model loading may depend on the user's environment.

faq.question: What should I measure during adoption?
faq.answer: Measure output token count, latency, cost, answer accuracy, and task-specific failure cases.
